title: OFAC Issues New Guidance on Maritime Sanctions Enforcement for Shell Company Structures
summary: U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) released updated guidance on January 13 clarifying enforcement standards for vessel ownership documentation involving shell company structures, following three recent enforcement actions against maritime insurers.
content:
The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued new guidance clarifying enforcement standards for maritime sanctions compliance, particularly regarding vessel ownership documentation involving shell company structures.

The guidance, released January 13, follows three recent enforcement actions against maritime insurers who failed to adequately verify beneficial ownership of sanctioned vessels. OFAC emphasized that the "50% rule" for ownership control determination applies to multi-tier shell company structures, requiring insurers to trace ownership chains through multiple jurisdictions.

Rachel Ng, Senior Maritime Compliance Analyst at Lloyd's Register, commented: "This guidance provides much-needed clarity on how OFAC expects insurers to apply the beneficial ownership standard to complex corporate structures. The key takeaway is that insurers can't rely on surface-level documentation - they need to trace ownership chains to ultimate beneficial owners."

The guidance also clarifies documentation requirements under 31 CFR 501, specifying that vessel registration transfers involving Panama, Liberia, and Marshall Islands registries require enhanced due diligence when shell company structures are involved.

Industry experts note that the guidance will significantly impact maritime insurance underwriting practices, particularly for vessel ownership transfers in jurisdictions with opaque corporate registry systems.

OFAC indicated that enforcement actions for violations occurring after January 13 will apply the clarified standards, giving insurers a 90-day compliance transition period.
